title: Finite-cone generation for all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficients
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] with its extended $\ell$-adic absolute-value topology, and a Noetherian scheme $X$ (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]). Let $\Lambda$ be the commutative condensed ring $S\mapsto C(S,\Omega)$ on profinite sets with the coherent topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], containing all continuous maps, without a finite-subextension restriction. For every scheme $Y$ over $X$, put $R_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_Y})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Say that an $R_Y$-module has a finite constant local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible] if on a pro-etale cover [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] it is $R_Y\otimes_{\Omega}V$ with $V$ a finitely presented scalar $\Omega$-module; these scalar modules are equivalently finite-dimensional vector spaces. Say that it is constructible if it has such models on a finite constructible locally closed scheme stratification [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset] of $Y$. Write $\mathcal B(X)$ for complexes with bounded constructible cohomology in this sense. Then $\mathcal B(X)$ is exactly the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$ containing $(a_!L)[0]$ for all constructible locally closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ and all $R_S$-modules $L$ that are lisse [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], meaning finite free on a pro-etale cover [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] of $S$. Here $a_!=i_*j_!$ for a factorization $S\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$ with $j$ open [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i$ closed, using the exact extension functors [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and pulled-back coefficients. Equivalently, an object belongs to $\mathcal B(X)$ if and only if it can be obtained up to isomorphism from finitely many such generators and zero by finitely many shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions. No passage to a common finite coefficient field, no coproduct closure and no completion is imposed; rank zero and $X=\varnothing$ are included.

source.place: Proof (1), opening lisse-generator reduction, as invoked in det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images proof (1),(2), integral and rational coefficients; all-continuous compatibility variant from the original AdmissibleTensorConstructibility proof, paragraph 3. Agent-stated adaptation, keeping the all-continuous ring separate.

proof.text: The scalar ring is $\Lambda(*)=\Omega$. A finitely presented vector space has a finite basis, so $R_T\otimes_\Omega V\cong R_T^r$, and conversely $R_T^r=R_T\otimes_\Omega\Omega^r$. Thus finite constant local models are precisely lisse modules, including rank zero [sk-def-sfb-constructible, def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. The underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Each locally closed subspace is Noetherian (intersect a descending chain of closed sets with the subspace), and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. These assertions also apply to every stratum used below.

source.place: Theorem 6.2(2): verification of the scheme and scalar-local-model hypotheses

proof.text: Verify the two coefficient hypotheses of [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations] for the actual all-continuous ring. Every ideal of the field $\Omega$ is zero or $\Omega$, hence is finitely presented; every finitely presented $\Omega$-module is finite free, hence has a length-zero finite projective resolution. For every extremally disconnected profinite $P$, the section ring $\Gamma(P,\Lambda)=C(P,\Omega)$ is an $\Omega$-vector space. A choice of basis identifies its tensor functor with a direct sum of copies of the identity, so it is flat over $\Omega$. This is t-admissibility as explicitly defined in the cited statement; it does not assert that continuous maps factor through a finite subfield. On any stratum $T$, that statement therefore identifies the cohomology of every dualizable object with finite constant local models. Its geometric hypothesis holds by step 1.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2); the field case of the two algebraic hypotheses

proof.text: Let $u:L\to M$ be a morphism of lisse $R_T$-modules on a stratum. By [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models], $L[0]$ and $M[0]$ are dualizable: on their respective trivializing covers they are scalar finite free complexes in degree zero. Derived scalar extension gives the same complexes since they are free. The cited statement makes their cone dualizable. The explicit cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] represents this cone by $L\xrightarrow{u}M$ in degrees $-1,0$, so its cohomology is $\ker u$ in degree $-1$, $\operatorname{coker}u$ in degree zero, and zero otherwise. Step 2 implies that these two sheaves have finite constant local models; by step 1 they are lisse. Thus kernels and cokernels are closed without any finite-field descent.

source.place: Theorem 4.13 and the stable-subcategory assertion after Definition 3.3, combined with Theorem 6.2(2)

proof.text: For a short exact sequence $0\to L\to E\to M\to0$ with lisse ends on $T$, first trivialize both ends on a common pro-etale cover. The epimorphism to the finite free $M$ splits after a further cover by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-free-epi-local-splitting]. On this cover the splitting identifies $E$ with $L\oplus M$: $(l,m)\mapsto l+s(m)$ has inverse $e\mapsto(e-s(\bar e),\bar e)$. Hence $E$ is finite free there and is lisse. The assertion includes a zero end.

source.place: Opening lisse reduction; extension closure as expanded in sk-lem-coefficient-heart.proof.md, Extensions paragraph

proof.text: Let $\mathscr A_c$ be the full isomorphism-closed class of constructible $R_X$-modules. It contains zero by the rank-zero model. For a map between two such modules, choose a common finite stratification by [lemma-constructible-common-refinement]; for an extension use a common stratification of its two ends. Pullbacks to the refined strata are exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], and coefficient pullbacks are the same $R_T$ by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. A pulled-back finite free model is still finite free (pullback preserves finite sums and the coefficient unit), so the restrictions of the known terms remain lisse. Steps 3 and 4 put the kernel, cokernel, or middle sheaf in the lisse class on every refined stratum. This proves the three closure properties of $\mathscr A_c$. All strata are topologically Noetherian by step 1, as required in step 3; no claim about a map between arbitrary locally finitely presented modules is used.

source.place: (1), common stratification and exact restriction; kernels/cokernels supplied here by HRS rather than finite-subfield descent

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] with ambient abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$ and class $\mathscr A_c$ of step 5. Its hypotheses are exactly zero, isomorphism closure, kernels, cokernels and extensions proved there. The bounded version of its conclusion identifies $\mathcal B(X)$ as a full replete triangulated subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category. In particular finite shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions of its objects stay in $\mathcal B(X)$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, bounded version; homology.tex Tag 0754, lemma-characterize-weak-serre-subcategory

proof.text: Every proposed generator belongs to $\mathcal B(X)$. Indeed write $a=i\circ j$ with $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], $j^*j_!L\cong L$ and the restriction of $j_!L$ to $Z\setminus S$ is zero; $i^*i_*j_!L\cong j_!L$, and the restriction to $X\setminus Z$ is zero. Coefficients agree by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Thus the three locally closed pieces $S$, $Z\setminus S$, $X\setminus Z$ give a finite constructible stratification with models $L,0,0$ (empty pieces can be omitted). The required complementary opens are quasi-compact since every subset of the Noetherian space is quasi-compact [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]. The two exact extension functors put this sheaf in degree zero with no other cohomology. It follows from step 6 that every finite construction from the proposed generators lies in $\mathcal B(X)$.

Conversely let $F$ be a constructible $R_X$-module. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration] to this $\Lambda$ and the Noetherian space $|X|$. It gives a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F$ with $Q_k=F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$, where $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ is open, $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ is reduced closed, and $L_k$ has a finite constant local model. Step 1 makes $L_k$ lisse. These are actual subquotients supplied by the cited statement, including the quasi-compactness hypotheses on its immersions.

Set $a_k=v_k\circ t_k$. The immersion $a_k$ is quasi-compact, since $t_k$ is a closed immersion and $v_k$ is quasi-compact by the statement of step 8. Hence [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor] gives a factorization $a_k=i_k\circ j_k$ with $j_k:S_k\hookrightarrow Z_k$ open and $i_k:Z_k\hookrightarrow X$ closed, so $a_k$ is an immersion of the kind used for the generators, and its underlying set $V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$ is locally closed, hence constructible in the Noetherian space $|X|$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. By [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence], the exact extension $v_{k!}(t_k)_*$ is canonically isomorphic to $i_{k*}j_{k!}$ for this factorization. Hence $Q_k[0]$ is one of the stated generators up to isomorphism. This uses the arbitrary-coefficient comparison, with inverse-image coefficients identified by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]; it does not replace the chosen $a_!$ by an unproved equality of functors. Since both functors are exact, the sheaf-level comparison applies termwise in degree zero.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09BM, 09BN, 09AH with sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI–03DJ and schemes.tex Tag 02V0; the existing locally-closed-extension-coherence node records the composite comparison, not a verbatim single-tag assertion.

proof.text: Let $\mathscr C$ be the class of objects obtainable from zero and finitely many proposed generators by finite shifts, triangle extensions, and isomorphisms. For each $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied in degree zero to $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to Q_k\to0$ supplies the triangle $F_{k-1}[0]\to F_k[0]\to Q_k[0]\to F_{k-1}[1]$. Induct on $k$, starting with $F_0[0]=0$: step 9 puts $Q_k[0]$ in $\mathscr C$, and the extension operation puts $F_k[0]$ in $\mathscr C$. Thus $F[0]\in\mathscr C$ after finitely many extensions. The argument with $r=0$ simply returns zero.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, applied to a sheaf short exact sequence in degree zero

proof.text: For $K\in\mathcal B(X)$ choose $a\le b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ and put $T_q=\tau_{\le q}K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $T_{a-1}$ is acyclic and $T_b\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $T_{a-1}\cong0$ and $T_b\cong K$ by localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each $q=a,\ldots,b$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(K)[-q]\to T_{q-1}[1]$. Step 10 and shift closure put its third term in $\mathscr C$. Induction from $T_{a-1}$ puts $T_b$, and hence $K$, in $\mathscr C$. Only the existence of these finite triangles is used, not any uniqueness assertion or convergence of an infinite tower.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, successive cohomology triangles; homology.tex Tag 0118, canonical truncation cohomology

proof.text: Steps 7 and 11 prove $\mathscr C=\mathcal B(X)$. Every full replete triangulated subcategory containing the generators contains $\mathscr C$, by induction on its finite construction expressions [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Conversely step 6 makes $\mathcal B(X)$ one of those subcategories. Therefore it is the smallest such subcategory, proving both formulations. The procedure uses at most $\sum_{q=a}^b r_q+(b-a+1)$ triangle extensions, where $r_q$ is a chosen finite filtration length for $H^q(K)$. An acyclic $K$ is already isomorphic to zero. When $X$ is empty all sheaves are zero, so the same conclusion holds with no generators. Throughout the coefficient ring is the original all-continuous ring; no common finite field, infinite coproduct, completion or retract operation is required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-41426f997 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's twelve steps and every cited statement in full, plus HRS Def 6.1, Thm 6.2(2) and Lemma 6.10 (PDF p.15). The statement is unchanged; the base item had no proof and live still has it unsplit. No new nodes, no cycle, proof_deps equal the union of the step uses, no SGA. The coefficient ring is the all-continuous C(-,Qbar_l) ring throughout and is never identified with the finite-subextension ring. Existing generation and heart nodes (det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation, det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure, lem-sfb-finite-field-stratified-generation) are for other rings, so this is not a duplicate. Steps 1-6 check: Lambda(*) is a field, so a finite constant local model is lisse; t-admissibility is trivial for a field; L[0] and M[0] are dualizable and their cone's H^{-1} and H^0 are ker and coker; a local splitting gives extensions; common refinement plus exact pullback make the constructible modules a weak Serre class, and the derived weak-Serre lemma makes B(X) triangulated. Step 7: open/closed identities give a generator with stratum models L, 0, 0. Steps 8, 10 and 11: the filtration node, the SES triangle and truncation triangles give a finite devissage. This re-derives lem-sfb-bounded-finite-model-generation; redundant but correct. Step 12: minimality is fine. Fault C1 in step 9: it used an open-then-closed factorization of a_k = v_k t_k without showing one exists. Fixed: a_k is quasi-compact, so the Mathlib leaf lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor gives a_k = i_k j_k, and its stratum is constructible (def-weil-constructible-subset); both ids added to uses and proof_deps.
